response.evidence: All prior research-only findings are closed in the corrected report. The corrected text explicitly scopes the work as investigation only with no implementation, preserves the STOP condition that the report does not authorize implementation, and requires owner approval before M1. It removes any reliance on live OFD refresh or access evasion: all four hosted bulk endpoints returned 403, cause unknown, and M1 ships a bundled OFD snapshot from a pinned, MIT-licensed inspected source with no live refresh promised; automatic refresh is deferred to a permitted intended-client fetch plus digest/schema validation. It mitigates the previous false-success and diameter unit concerns: it states no inspected application was physically demonstrated on the intended NTAG215/OpenSpool workflow and prescribes read/inspect/capacity-check/write/fresh-read/decode-compare with RF-loss and failure tests; the 1.75 mm diameter writes decimal 1.75 and legacy 175 is rejected unless corrected. It labels the NTAG215 payload/NDEF calculations as reproducible serialization/header calculations from payload-size-calculation.json, not runtime or physical-write evidence. It defers OpenPrintTag/OPT to separate NFC-V hardware and makes phone/model/tag/firmware identification a start-of-M1 step rather than a prerequisite for approving research. Remaining acceptance items (e.g., measuring Room/FTS size, warm-search p95, independent-reader persistence, network capture) are future M1 execution criteria and are explicitly identified as unmeasured planning budgets, not defects in the research conclusion.
